metric.definition: In grid regions with a capacity market, the auction-cleared price paid per megawatt-day for generators to guarantee availability years ahead. Passed through to large loads, it is a fixed overhead on every megawatt-hour a facility consumes, separate from the energy price itself.

reading.body:
Capacity market clearing price is the auction-cleared price paid per megawatt-day for generators to guarantee availability years ahead, in grid regions that run a capacity market, passed through to large loads as a fixed overhead on every megawatt-hour consumed, separate from the energy price itself.

Data center demand growth has pushed capacity auctions in constrained regions to record clearing prices, a cost that lands on operators as a non-energy surcharge. The data draws a specific structural distinction, energy-only markets have no equivalent charge and instead expose loads to scarcity pricing during extreme events, meaning the two market structures trade predictable overhead against price volatility rather than one simply costing more than the other. PJM Interconnection is named as the source publishing auction results directly after each delivery-year auction.

It groups with approval to energize versus queued load, behind-the-meter generation, interconnection queue position and wait, and power purchase agreements under Power and grid, the metrics collectively tracking how a facility's power costs and access are actually determined.
